title: 발키리의 문
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create ONE finished story-stage landscape illustration, without any title or lettering. Opaque wide 16:9 at the largest available landscape resolution, intended for downscaling to 640x360 and display at 360-480px width. Reference 1 is the game's painted pixel-art style anchor; reference 2 is its story painting style; reference 3 is this realm's palette, architecture and landmarks. All are reference inputs, not edit targets. Match the crisp visible painted pixel clusters and stepped silhouettes, rich but controlled colour, layered fantasy depth; no photographic or smooth 3D rendering. Cohesive nine-picture set rules: wide level establishing view, one dominant landmark centred horizontally in the MIDDLE THIRD, skyline/horizon around 70-74% image height in the LOWER THIRD, key environmental light from UPPER LEFT, midtone readability with dark blue-violet shadows, moderate saturation and contrast comparable to the other realms. Simple large shapes readable in a thumbnail. The outermost 3% on every side must be low-detail calm scenery safe for an 8px frame overlap, but DO NOT draw a frame. Keep the entire landmark in view. No people, human faces, humanoid figures, statues, letters, text-like decoration, glyphs, runes, numerals, logo, watermark, UI, borders or frames. No text anywhere. Stage 2, take A. ASGARD: a monumental GOLDEN GATE with an unmistakable pair of broad sculpted WINGS built into the two gateposts, and a compact spired GOLDEN CASTLE directly behind. The wing carvings are purely feathers, no angels or figures. Several luminous columns of light FALL from high clouds around the gate. Take A: direct frontal approach across a short pale-stone causeway, central gate opening clear and castle visible above it. Cool blue-grey clouds, warm ivory-gold stone and quiet cyan depth from realm reference. Broad open sky fills upper two thirds except central gate and castle silhouette; a low cloud-sea horizon at y72%, NO high mountain skyline. Upper-left diffuse golden daylight clearly illuminates left surfaces; vertical light pillars are secondary. No decorative runes, medallion symbols or lettering.
